Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the quick note and for keeping this lightweight. We signed up through the quickstart flow this morning. Happy to do a 30m demo to understand how Redwood would fit into our checkout conversational assistant. A few quick answers up front to help scope the call: 

- Primary use case: live checkout assistance (product recommendations + address and payment helper) for desktop and mobile web.
- Expected volume: ~1.2M pageviews/month; estimate ~40k conversations/month initially, peak concurrent sessions ~120.
- Latency target: ideally <300ms token latency for user-facing flows.
- Timeline: we want a pilot running in prod in Q1 (Jan) — evaluation + POC in Nov-Dec.

I attached a small csv with sample daily traffic for September.

Availability: I can do Tue 10/17 10:30–11:00 PT or Wed 10/18 after 13:00 PT. Let me know what works.

—Emma

Hi Emma — thanks, that traffic file is helpful. Quick follow-ups before we lock a slot so we focus the demo: 

1) Is the checkout assistant currently CPU-based (serverless containers) or do you already run any GPU-hosted models? If CPU, what's your typical request size (tokens in/out)?
2) Can you share whether payment/address helpers require PII processing or do you redact/mask on the client side? This affects private deployment options and data retention.
3) For peak concurrency ~120, is that sustained or bursty (e.g., spikes during promotions)?

We can do Tue 10/17 10:30 PT — I have a 30m slot open. Monica (CC) will join to cover onboarding/pilot options and sandbox access. If that time doesn't work, share any other 30m windows and we’ll accommodate.

Agenda proposal (30m): 1) quick product fit (10m), 2) traffic/profile/SLAs (10m), 3) next steps & pilot checklist (10m).

Thanks — Karthik
Director, Solutions

Thanks — quick answers inline: 
1) CPU-based today (serverless containers). Typical request payload: ~120 tokens in / 35 tokens out on average.
2) Payment data is tokenized at payment provider; address fields are partially redacted before they hit our app (we mask last 4 digits of phone, etc). We prefer not to send raw payment info to third parties.
3) Bursty — mostly black-friday-style promotional spikes (can 3–4x baseline for a few hours).

10/17 10:30 PT works for me. Please send calendar invite.
